vocabulary.wordCount: {count, plural, =0 {No words} one {# word} other {# words}}
vocabulary.bulkPasteHint: One word per line: lemma, translation, and optionally part of speech — separated by tabs (pasted from a spreadsheet) or " - ".

sykkel	bicycle	noun
sykle	to cycle
vocabulary.bulkPasteRowCount: {count, plural, =0 {No words detected} one {# word detected} other {# words detected}}
vocabulary.bulkPasteSubmit: {count, plural, =0 {Add words} one {Add # word} other {Add # words}}

vocabulary.deleteConfirmDescription: "{lemma}" will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
vocabulary.examplesHint: Use ___ where the word goes in the sentence.

exercises.empty: No exercises yet. Add the first one.
exercises.deleteConfirmDescription: "{title}" will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
exercises.instructionsPlaceholder: Optional instructions shown to the student
exercises.instructionsHint: Required — an exercise without instructions cannot be published.
exercises.hintPlaceholder: Optional hint the student can reveal
exercises.mcgContextPlaceholder: Optional line shown above the questions
exercises.mcgSharedOptionsHint: The answer column every question uses, e.g. Riktig / Galt. A question can replace it with options of its own.
exercises.mcgQuestionsHint: All questions are answered and checked together as one block.
exercises.mcgNoSharedOptions: Add shared options above, or give this question its own.
exercises.mcgExplanationPlaceholder: Why this answer is right (shown after checking)
exercises.fibTextPlaceholder: Use ___1___, ___2___ for blanks, e.g. Jeg ___1___ norsk.
exercises.saQuestionPlaceholder: e.g. When did Anne hear the news?
exercises.saContextPlaceholder: A passage or hint shown with the question
exercises.saReferenceAnswerHint: The model answer. Also graded against: an exact match passes automatically.
exercises.saAcceptedHint: Separated by |, not commas — these answers often contain a comma. Each one the learner may write; the closest is used to mark their answer.
exercises.saAcceptedPlaceholder: at han jobbet som elektriker | han jobbet som elektriker
exercises.saTrialHint: Type an answer the way a learner would. You'll see exactly what they'd see.
exercises.saTrialMarkedWrong: Marked wrong ({score}%) with the mistake shown word by word:
exercises.saTrialReview: Too far from the key — this goes to you for manual grading. Add it below if it should pass.
exercises.wtPromptPlaceholder: e.g. Write a short reader letter about…
exercises.wtTopicsHint: Let the learner choose one topic to write about
exercises.ssSentencePlaceholder: e.g. Lars har aldri likt Lotte.
exercises.ssSourceSentenceHelp: When set, the learner sees this one and rebuilds the target sentence; the target stays hidden until the answer is checked.
exercises.ssTokensHint: Type each word and choose the field it belongs to; order within a field follows this list
exercises.fibRationaleHint: Shown to the student after checking — why the answer fits and why other options don't.
exercises.fibRationaleExplanationPlaceholder: e.g. A statement is introduced by «at».
exercises.fibRationaleNotePlaceholder: why it does or doesn't fit
exercises.fibRationaleAttached: Explanation matrix attached — shown after checking
exercises.wbfWordBankHint: Comma-separated. Every blank of every sentence is chosen from this bank.
exercises.wbfWordBankPlaceholder: show off, boast, clicked with, get to know
exercises.wbfSentencesHint: Mark blanks with ___1___, ___2___ … numbered within each sentence.
exercises.wbfSentencePlaceholder: I hate it when people ___1___ all the time.
exercises.toLinesHint: Type them in the right order — the learner sees them shuffled.
exercises.toLinePlaceholder: Hi, I’m Marina. What brings you here?
exercises.mpVariantHint: Sentence halves number the left column 1, 2, 3 … and letter the right A, B, C …
exercises.ecSentencesHint: Split each sentence into parts with | — the learner taps a part to rewrite it. Then name the faulty part by its number.
exercises.ecChunksPlaceholder: I could see | that the more | I talked to Sue | she was warming up with me

levels.heading: How is it structured?
levels.subtitle: Levels group modules. This maps 1:1 to how students see the course in the reader.
levels.cefrDesc: Six-level scaffold, ready to prune. Matches the student reader.
levels.customDesc: Define your own progression and naming.
levels.singleDesc: One flat list of modules — no level grouping.

starter.cefrDesc: 1 level, 1 module, 4 lessons (vocab, reading, listening, practice).
starter.cloneDesc: Copy structure & content from a course you already have.

spans.needsBody: Save the anchor text first to annotate it.
spans.noList: This module has no vocabulary list yet — add one to annotate lexis.
spans.noRules: This Leksjon has no grammar rules yet. Add a rule to its grammar lesson, then it can be annotated here.
spans.firstVocabWarning: This text still highlights {count, plural, one {# glossary word} other {# glossary words}} automatically. The first lexis annotation switches that off: from then on students see only the words you annotate here.
spans.explainer: The student sees the words highlighted, with a marker that opens the explanation.
spans.helpVocab: — underlines the word and opens its dictionary card. The first lexis annotation switches off the automatic glossary highlighting in this text: from then on only annotated words are underlined.
spans.helpGrammar: — highlights the passage and points it at a rule from this Leksjon’s grammar lesson.
spans.helpChunk: — highlights a set expression and shows your note. No dictionary, no rule.
spans.helpAnchor: An annotation is anchored to this exact stretch of text. Edit the text under it and it can lose its anchor — the student stops seeing it, and it appears in the list below, where you can reattach it.
spans.overlapError: This selection overlaps an annotation of the same type. Adjust the selection, or remove the other one first.
spans.errorEmpty: Select some of the anchor text to annotate it.
spans.errorCrossesParagraph: An annotation has to stay inside one paragraph. Shorten the selection.
spans.errorTooLong: That selection is too long to annotate — 400 characters at most.
spans.caption: {count, plural, one {# annotation} other {# annotations}} in this text.
spans.brokenTitle: {count, plural, one {# annotation lost its anchor} other {# annotations lost their anchor}}
spans.brokenBody: The text moved under them, so students no longer see them. Reattach or remove each one.
spans.brokenRef: Its word or rule was deleted.
spans.reanchorGone: This text is no longer in the body.
spans.reanchorAmbiguous: This text now occurs more than once — select it again to reattach.
spans.unmarkConfirmTitle: Remove this word from the lesson glossary?
spans.unmarkConfirmBody: “{lemma}” stops being part of this lesson's glossary, and its annotations in this text go with it. The module keeps the word, so other lessons and the unit vocabulary list are unaffected.
spans.unmarked: Word removed from the lesson glossary.

list.emptyBody: A course is the top-level container. Each has CEFR levels, modules and lessons. Start blank or from a template.

discardDraft.title: Discard this draft?
discardDraft.description: The draft and all its content will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.

unpublish.title: Unpublish this course?
unpublish.description: Students will see a "Course paused" banner. No new enrolments will be accepted. You can re-publish at any time.

archive.title: Archive this course?
archive.description: The course will be hidden from the catalogue and enrolment will be closed. All content and student progress is kept — you can restore it at any time.
archive.enrollmentWarning: {count, plural, one {# student is} other {# students are}} currently enrolled — they keep access until you restore or delete the course.

restore.title: Restore this course?
restore.description: The course will be returned to its previous state.

deleteForever.title: Delete "{title}"?
deleteForever.description: All content, lessons, and student history for this course will be permanently deleted after 30 days.
deleteForever.contentCounts: This will delete {modules, plural, one {# module} other {# modules}} and {lessons, plural, one {# lesson} other {# lessons}}.
deleteForever.steerToArchive: Consider archiving instead — it keeps everything and can be undone.

reviewPublish.title: Review & publish
reviewPublish.description: Pick what to make live. The course and each module are published separately — modules go first, so the course never points at material students cannot open.
reviewPublish.allPublished: Everything is published. Nothing to release.
